paper_title: Direct and indirect loop equations in lattice Yang-Mills theory (Liu, 2026, JHEP)
deeper_reasoning_1:
\textbf{Claim.}
For every finite canonical target set \(S_0\), if the returned direct rows \(E_{\mathrm{dir}}(S_0)\) are a row-independent basis of the operational generator set consisting of retained plaquette-cut Schwinger-Dyson rows and retained SU(2) trace-collision rows, then
\[
\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb{Q}(\lambda)}E_{\mathrm{dir}}(S_0)
=
R_{\mathrm{dir}}(D,S_0).
\]
Thus the direct construction is complete exactly relative to the finite target set and the paper's retention rule.

\textbf{Premises.}
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
(P1) & S_0\text{ is a finite set of canonical SU(2) Wilson-loop classes.}\\
(P2) & \mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{pc}}(S_0)=\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{dir}}^{\mathrm{SD}}(S_0).\\
(P3) & \mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{tc}}(S_0)=\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{dir}}^{\mathrm{Tr}}(S_0).\\
(P4) & R_{\mathrm{dir}}(D,S_0):=
\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb{Q}(\lambda)}
\left(\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{dir}}^{\mathrm{SD}}(S_0)\cup
\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{dir}}^{\mathrm{Tr}}(S_0)\right).\\
(P5) & \mathcal{G}_{\mathrm{dir}}(S_0):=
\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{pc}}(S_0)\cup\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{tc}}(S_0).\\
(P6) & E_{\mathrm{dir}}(S_0)\text{ is row-independent and }
\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb{Q}(\lambda)}E_{\mathrm{dir}}(S_0)
=
\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb{Q}(\lambda)}\mathcal{G}_{\mathrm{dir}}(S_0).
\end{array}
\]

\textbf{Derivation.}
The operational direct generator span is
\begin{align}
\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb{Q}(\lambda)}\mathcal{G}_{\mathrm{dir}}(S_0)
&=
\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb{Q}(\lambda)}
\left(\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{pc}}(S_0)\cup\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{tc}}(S_0)\right)
&&\text{by (P5)}\\
&=
\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb{Q}(\lambda)}
\left(\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{dir}}^{\mathrm{SD}}(S_0)\cup
\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{dir}}^{\mathrm{Tr}}(S_0)\right)
&&\text{by (P2), (P3)}\\
&=
R_{\mathrm{dir}}(D,S_0)
&&\text{by (P4)}.
\end{align}
Since \(E_{\mathrm{dir}}(S_0)\) has the same span as this operational generator set,
\begin{align}
\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb{Q}(\lambda)}E_{\mathrm{dir}}(S_0)
&=
\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb{Q}(\lambda)}\mathcal{G}_{\mathrm{dir}}(S_0)
&&\text{by (P6)}\\
&=
R_{\mathrm{dir}}(D,S_0)
&&\text{by the previous chain}.
\end{align}
Because \(E_{\mathrm{dir}}(S_0)\) is row-independent by (P6), it is a basis of \(R_{\mathrm{dir}}(D,S_0)\).

\textbf{Final Result.}
\[
\boxed{
E_{\mathrm{dir}}(S_0)\text{ is a complete independent basis of }R_{\mathrm{dir}}(D,S_0)
}
\]
\hfill\(\blacksquare\)
deeper_reasoning_2:
\textbf{Claim.}
Let \(S_0\subset S_1\) be finite canonical loop sets. Write a row-spanning direct matrix in \(S_1\) as
\[
A_x\mathbf{x}+A_y\mathbf{y}=0,
\]
where \(\mathbf{x}\) indexes \(S_0\) and \(\mathbf{y}\) indexes \(S_1\setminus S_0\). Then the projected target-space row space is exactly
\[
P(D,S_0,S_1)=
\left\{u^TA_x:\ u^TA_y=0\right\},
\]
and the indirect quotient has dimension
\[
\dim I(D,S_0,S_1)
=
\dim P(D,S_0,S_1)-\dim R_{\mathrm{dir}}(D,S_0)
\]
whenever \(R_{\mathrm{dir}}(D,S_0)\subseteq P(D,S_0,S_1)\).

\textbf{Premises.}
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
(P1) & A_x\mathbf{x}+A_y\mathbf{y}=0\text{ has rows spanning }R_{\mathrm{dir}}(D,S_1).\\
(P2) & K:=\{u:\ u^TA_y=0\}.\\
(P3) & P(D,S_0,S_1):=\{u^TA_x:\ u\in K\}.\\
(P4) & R_{\mathrm{dir}}(D,S_0)\subseteq P(D,S_0,S_1).\\
(P5) & I(D,S_0,S_1):=P(D,S_0,S_1)/R_{\mathrm{dir}}(D,S_0).\\
(P6) & \dim(V/U)=\dim V-\dim U\text{ if }U\subseteq V\text{ are finite-dimensional.}
\end{array}
\]

\textbf{Derivation.}
For any row-combination vector \(u\),
\begin{align}
u^T(A_x\mathbf{x}+A_y\mathbf{y})
&=u^TA_x\mathbf{x}+u^TA_y\mathbf{y}.
\end{align}
If \(u\in K\), then \(u^TA_y=0\), so this row combination contains no auxiliary coordinate:
\begin{align}
u^T(A_x\mathbf{x}+A_y\mathbf{y})
&=u^TA_x\mathbf{x}.
\end{align}
Hence every \(u\in K\) gives a target-only row \(u^TA_x\mathbf{x}=0\). Conversely, a row combination that is target-only has zero coefficient on every auxiliary coordinate, hence satisfies \(u^TA_y=0\), so its target coefficient row lies in \(\{u^TA_x:\ u^TA_y=0\}\). Therefore
\[
P(D,S_0,S_1)=\{u^TA_x:\ u^TA_y=0\}.
\]
Using the quotient definition,
\begin{align}
\dim I(D,S_0,S_1)
&=\dim\left(P(D,S_0,S_1)/R_{\mathrm{dir}}(D,S_0)\right)
&&\text{by (P5)}\\
&=\dim P(D,S_0,S_1)-\dim R_{\mathrm{dir}}(D,S_0)
&&\text{by (P4), (P6)}.
\end{align}

\textbf{Final Result.}
\[
\boxed{
P(D,S_0,S_1)=\{u^TA_x:\ u^TA_y=0\},
\qquad
\dim I=\dim P-\dim R_{\mathrm{dir}}(D,S_0)
}
\]
\hfill\(\blacksquare\)
deeper_reasoning_4:
\textbf{Claim.}
Assume the two-dimensional loop-count and equation-ratio ansatz
\[
N_{\mathrm{loop}}^{(2\mathrm{D})}(L)\simeq A_{2\mathrm{D}}L^{-2}3^L,
\qquad
\frac{N_{\mathrm{eqn}}^{(2\mathrm{D})}(L)}{N_{\mathrm{loop}}^{(2\mathrm{D})}(L)}
\simeq 1-\frac{c}{L^{\delta}},
\]
with \(A_{2\mathrm{D}}>0\), \(c>0\), and \(\delta>0\). Then the direct-equation residual dimension
\[
d_{\mathrm{dir}}(L):=N_{\mathrm{loop}}^{(2\mathrm{D})}(L)-N_{\mathrm{eqn}}^{(2\mathrm{D})}(L)
\]
has the asymptotic form
\[
d_{\mathrm{dir}}(L)\simeq A_{2\mathrm{D}}c\,L^{-(2+\delta)}3^L.
\]
Thus the constrained fraction tends to one, but the absolute residual still grows with exponential base \(3\).

\textbf{Premises.}
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
(P1) & N_{\mathrm{loop}}^{(2\mathrm{D})}(L)\simeq A_{2\mathrm{D}}L^{-2}3^L.\\
(P2) & R(L):=N_{\mathrm{eqn}}^{(2\mathrm{D})}(L)/N_{\mathrm{loop}}^{(2\mathrm{D})}(L).\\
(P3) & R(L)\simeq 1-c/L^{\delta}.\\
(P4) & d_{\mathrm{dir}}(L):=N_{\mathrm{loop}}^{(2\mathrm{D})}(L)-N_{\mathrm{eqn}}^{(2\mathrm{D})}(L).\\
(P5) & A_{2\mathrm{D}}>0,\quad c>0,\quad \delta>0.
\end{array}
\]

\textbf{Derivation.}
Using \(N_{\mathrm{eqn}}^{(2\mathrm{D})}(L)=R(L)N_{\mathrm{loop}}^{(2\mathrm{D})}(L)\),
\begin{align}
d_{\mathrm{dir}}(L)
&=N_{\mathrm{loop}}^{(2\mathrm{D})}(L)-N_{\mathrm{eqn}}^{(2\mathrm{D})}(L)
&&\text{by (P4)}\\
&=N_{\mathrm{loop}}^{(2\mathrm{D})}(L)\left(1-R(L)\right)\\
&\simeq
\left(A_{2\mathrm{D}}L^{-2}3^L\right)
\left(1-\left(1-\frac{c}{L^{\delta}}\right)\right)
&&\text{by (P1), (P3)}\\
&=
A_{2\mathrm{D}}c\,L^{-(2+\delta)}3^L.
\end{align}
Dividing by the loop count gives
\[
\frac{d_{\mathrm{dir}}(L)}{N_{\mathrm{loop}}^{(2\mathrm{D})}(L)}
\simeq \frac{c}{L^\delta},
\]
which tends to \(0\) because \(\delta>0\). The absolute residual retains the factor \(3^L\), so the direct equations can asymptotically cover almost all variables without making the independent remainder polynomially small.

\textbf{Final Result.}
\[
\boxed{
d_{\mathrm{dir}}(L)\simeq A_{2\mathrm{D}}c\,L^{-(2+\delta)}3^L,
\qquad
\frac{d_{\mathrm{dir}}(L)}{N_{\mathrm{loop}}^{(2\mathrm{D})}(L)}
\simeq \frac{c}{L^\delta}
}
\]
\hfill\(\blacksquare\)
deeper_reasoning_6:
\textbf{Claim.}
Suppose \(E_{\mathrm{dir}}\) is a basis of \(R_{\mathrm{dir}}(D,S_0)\) and \(E_{\mathrm{ind}}\) is a representative basis of
\[
P(D,S_0,S_1)/R_{\mathrm{dir}}(D,S_0).
\]
Then \(E_{\mathrm{dir}}\cup E_{\mathrm{ind}}\) is an independent basis of the combined projected constraint space \(P(D,S_0,S_1)\). Hence the number of dynamically free target variables after direct and indirect constraints is
\[
|S_0|-\dim R_{\mathrm{dir}}(D,S_0)-|E_{\mathrm{ind}}|.
\]

\textbf{Premises.}
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
(P1) & E_{\mathrm{dir}}\text{ is a basis of }R:=R_{\mathrm{dir}}(D,S_0).\\
(P2) & P:=P(D,S_0,S_1).\\
(P3) & R\subseteq P.\\
(P4) & E_{\mathrm{ind}}=\{v_1,\ldots,v_q\}\subset P.\\
(P5) & \{v_1+R,\ldots,v_q+R\}\text{ is a basis of }P/R.\\
(P6) & S_0\text{ is finite, so the target coordinate space has dimension }|S_0|.
\end{array}
\]

\textbf{Derivation.}
To prove spanning, let \(p\in P\). Since the quotient classes of \(E_{\mathrm{ind}}\) span \(P/R\), there are coefficients \(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_q\in\mathbb{Q}(\lambda)\) such that
\[
p+R=\sum_{i=1}^{q}\alpha_i(v_i+R).
\]
Hence
\[
p-\sum_{i=1}^{q}\alpha_i v_i\in R.
\]
Because \(E_{\mathrm{dir}}\) spans \(R\), the difference is a linear combination of rows in \(E_{\mathrm{dir}}\). Thus \(p\) is a linear combination of \(E_{\mathrm{dir}}\cup E_{\mathrm{ind}}\), so the union spans \(P\).

To prove independence, suppose
\[
\sum_{e\in E_{\mathrm{dir}}}\beta_e e+\sum_{i=1}^{q}\alpha_i v_i=0.
\]
Passing to the quotient by \(R\), the first sum vanishes and gives
\[
\sum_{i=1}^{q}\alpha_i(v_i+R)=0+R.
\]
The quotient classes in (P5) are independent, so \(\alpha_i=0\) for all \(i\). The remaining equation is
\[
\sum_{e\in E_{\mathrm{dir}}}\beta_e e=0,
\]
and \(E_{\mathrm{dir}}\) is independent by (P1), so every \(\beta_e=0\). Therefore \(E_{\mathrm{dir}}\cup E_{\mathrm{ind}}\) is independent.

Consequently,
\begin{align}
\dim P
&=\dim R+|E_{\mathrm{ind}}|,\\
d_{\mathrm{free}}
&=|S_0|-\dim P\\
&=|S_0|-\dim R_{\mathrm{dir}}(D,S_0)-|E_{\mathrm{ind}}|.
\end{align}

\textbf{Final Result.}
\[
\boxed{
E_{\mathrm{dir}}\cup E_{\mathrm{ind}}\text{ is an independent basis of }P(D,S_0,S_1)
}
\]
\[
\boxed{
d_{\mathrm{free}}=|S_0|-\dim R_{\mathrm{dir}}(D,S_0)-|E_{\mathrm{ind}}|
}
\]
\hfill\(\blacksquare\)
deeper_reasoning_7:
\textbf{Claim.}
Raw plaquette-cut generation counts are not basis counts. In the two paper examples,
\[
4\mapsto 3,\qquad 10\mapsto 6,
\]
so row-rank reduction is mathematically necessary before claiming an independent direct equation basis.

\textbf{Premises.}
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
(P1) & W_1:=W[C_1,a,b,-a,-b,a,C_2]\text{ has }2\text{ cuts and }2\text{ raw insertions per cut.}\\
(P2) & W_1\text{ has }1\text{ equivalence among the raw candidates.}\\
(P3) & W_2:=W[C_1,a,b,-a,-b,a,b,-a,-b,C_2]\text{ has }5\text{ cuts and }2\text{ raw insertions per cut.}\\
(P4) & W_2\text{ has }4\text{ equivalences among the raw candidates.}\\
(P5) & n_{\mathrm{raw}}:=2n_{\mathrm{cut}}.\\
(P6) & n_{\mathrm{ind}}:=n_{\mathrm{raw}}-n_{\mathrm{eq}}.\\
(P7) & \text{A basis count must count independent rows, not merely generated rows.}
\end{array}
\]

\textbf{Derivation.}
For the first word,
\begin{align}
n_{\mathrm{raw}}(W_1)
&=2\cdot 2
&&\text{by (P1), (P5)}\\
&=4,\\
n_{\mathrm{ind}}(W_1)
&=n_{\mathrm{raw}}(W_1)-1
&&\text{by (P2), (P6)}\\
&=3.
\end{align}
Thus \(W_1\) has raw-to-independent loss
\[
4-3=1.
\]
For the second word,
\begin{align}
n_{\mathrm{raw}}(W_2)
&=2\cdot 5
&&\text{by (P3), (P5)}\\
&=10,\\
n_{\mathrm{ind}}(W_2)
&=n_{\mathrm{raw}}(W_2)-4
&&\text{by (P4), (P6)}\\
&=6.
\end{align}
Thus \(W_2\) has raw-to-independent loss
\[
10-6=4.
\]
Therefore a construction that only enumerates raw plaquette cuts overcounts the independent direct constraints in both examples. By (P7), the direct target \(E_{\mathrm{dir}}\) must be certified by linear independence or row rank after trace and canonical equivalences have been applied.

\textbf{Final Result.}
\[
\boxed{
W_1:\ 4\text{ raw candidates}\mapsto 3\text{ independent candidates},
\qquad
W_2:\ 10\text{ raw candidates}\mapsto 6\text{ independent candidates}
}
\]
\[
\boxed{
\text{row-rank reduction is required before raw generator counts can define }E_{\mathrm{dir}}
}
\]
\hfill\(\blacksquare\)
